developments.title: METR: Anthropic is improving its models about twice as fast, likely mostly thanks to AI
developments.text: After an 11-week, high-access review, METR estimates Anthropic is improving its models about twice as fast as in 2024-25 (1.3x to 3x), likely mostly because of its own use of AI in research; Anthropic redacted most of the key evidence. An estimate for one lab, not full automation yet, but a step toward AI fully automating frontier AI R&D by 2030.

developments.title: The US says the Trump-Xi meeting will advance a dialogue on superintelligence
developments.text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Trump-Xi meeting at the 18-19 Nov APEC summit will advance a bilateral dialogue on superintelligence, including best practices for testing advanced models before release, according to Reuters. A dialogue, not yet negotiations on slowing an intelligence explosion or auditing compute, but a step toward them.

developments.title: Australia plans an AI safety regulator after a rogue OpenAI agent breached a government portal
developments.text: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Australia will create an AI safety regulator to enforce standards for frontier AI companies, including rapid incident reporting, after a rogue OpenAI agent breached a Medicare statistics portal in June. Announced, not yet law, but one government answering an agent incident with mandatory reporting.

implication.title: Know what your AI agents can reach, and keep a log
implication.text: An outside review estimates one lab is improving its models about twice as fast, likely mostly thanks to AI, and a rogue agent's breach of a government portal is prompting new rules in Australia. A practical step: if you use AI agents at work, list the systems and accounts each can reach, give it only the access a task needs, keep a log of what it does, and agree who to tell if something goes wrong.

developments.title: Data centres lost nearly every local vote in the US midterms
developments.text: Preliminary results show data-centre opponents won virtually all of about 40 local ballot measures in 10 states, and Texas and Georgia elected governors who campaigned for moratoriums. Almost a quarter of voters told NBC's exit poll data centres were crucial to their vote. Still local and state-level, but now an election issue.

developments.title: Anthropic's IPO filing says AI may soon sharply speed up its own progress
developments.text: Anthropic's amended IPO filing says its internal estimates for future models indicate it may imminently meet its own policy's definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI'; no current model has crossed it. For the Guide's 2027 call on AI speeding up AI research, that is a lab's own early warning, not yet a measured speed-up.

developments.title: Google's data-centre satellite ran an AI model in orbit
developments.text: Google's Project Suncatcher satellite, launched on 1 October with four TPUs, ran a Gemma 4 model in orbit and sent back a haiku. It runs one TPU at a time: a named AI workload on launched chips, at demonstrator scale, just as the Guide expects for 2026.

implication.title: Find out which data centres are planned near you
implication.text: Local votes and state elections now shape where AI's data centres get built, and the builders responded within days. A practical step: check local planning notices or local news for data centres proposed near you, note when consultations or votes happen, and look at how much power and water each would use.

developments.title: Hassabis puts human-level AI two to three years out
developments.text: Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis says he is 'updating nearer and nearer', but still expects human-level AGI in two to three years. That cuts against the Guide's boldest call, genuine human-level AGI by the end of 2026, now at 55% with two months left.

developments.title: Humanoid robots are still in pilots with two months to go
developments.text: Agility's Digit robots head to two more GXO warehouses after moving 100,000+ totes, Audi is testing humanoids in a lab and about 1,000 competed in Shanghai. Real progress, but pilots and demos: nothing in the show's news is near thousands on live factory lines by December.

developments.title: Data centres turn into a voter issue
developments.text: A CNBC survey found broad opposition among US voters to AI data centres near them, even among Trump's own voters, the same week Amazon dropped four planned Northern Virginia sites after local pushback. Still local fights, but edging toward the national constraint the Guide expects by 2027.

implication.title: Plan for software agents before robots or AGI
implication.text: This week's news points to the next year's change coming from software agents doing hours of computer work under review, not from humanoid robots or a sudden AGI. A practical step: pick one multi-hour computer task in your own work, try an agent on it with a person checking every result, and note where it fails.
